system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the fatigue crack growth rate in rolling contact fatigue: da/dN = C(ΔK)^m, where da/dN is crack growth per cycle, ΔK is stress intensity factor range, and C, m are material constants. Inner-race spalling initiates at microcracks and propagates under cyclic Hertzian stress; early-stage growth is slow and subcritical, detectable as increasing high-frequency vibration energy in specific bands before amplitude exceeds alarm threshold.
USER CONSTRAINT: 1 kHz vibration sensor sampling rate sufficient to capture bearing defect frequencies and early-stage crack signatures
CALCULATED: 14-day warning window aligns with typical bearing crack growth rate from ~0.1mm to spall-failure size under 350 kW load

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components: Existing 1 kHz vibration sensor, signal processing module (off-the-shelf DSP with FFT capability), SCADA interface module. Materials: Standard industrial-grade electronics. Instruments: Vibration sensor (already installed), signal analyzer for validation. Procedure: Process vibration data to calculate kurtosis factor of acceleration signal in 2-10 kHz band; implement running average over 24-hour window; compare against threshold in SCADA logic.
USER CONSTRAINT: Must use existing 1 kHz vibration sensor
ASSUMPTION: DSP module can be programmed to calculate kurtosis from 1 kHz time-series data

STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — Standard practice uses simple vibration amplitude alarms with no warning. This approach requires additional signal processing but uses existing hardware. Implementation burden is low (software-only change), operability matches existing SCADA, maintenance is nil (no new hardware), and cost class is minimal (software development only). Worth it because it provides actionable warning window while using existing infrastructure.
USER CONSTRAINT: Must use existing 1 kHz vibration sensor and 1 Hz SCADA logging

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install test bearing with known defect size progression on 350 kW fan drive. Record vibration data continuously while monitoring bearing condition. Process data using proposed kurtosis algorithm. Instruments: Vibration sensor, bearing condition analyzer, data logger. Pass/fail threshold: Algorithm must detect defect initiation at least 14 days before bearing reaches failure vibration level (defined as 10 mm/s RMS) with no more than 2 false alarms per year. Duration: 6 months of continuous testing with multiple bearing failure events.
USER CONSTRAINT: Fire at least 14 days warning
USER CONSTRAINT: Produce no more than 2 false alarms per year
CALCULATED: 10 mm/s RMS failure threshold based on industrial vibration standards for 350 kW machinery

DESIGN: Kurtosis factor of vibration acceleration in 2-10 kHz band, with 24-hour running average
THRESHOLD: 5.0 (normal bearing kurtosis is ~3.0, rises with defect presence)
TEST: As described above in EXECUTABLE TEST section
